title: IT Admin for the AI Workforce — Sarthak Aggarwal, Decawork
talk_summary: Sarthak Aggarwal argues that autonomous agents should be treated as managed workers with identity, delegated authority, scoped capabilities, and deterministic policy gates outside the model. The core mechanism is separating a trusted planner (which produces a typed, logged plan) from an executor that processes untrusted evidence and can only request pre-approved actions through a policy gate.

takeaways.technique: Plan/execute privilege separation with policy gate
takeaways.what_they_do: A trusted planner converts authenticated intent into a typed, logged plan before seeing any untrusted evidence; the executor processes untrusted content and every action becomes a typed request checked against plan capability and risk by a policy gate.
takeaways.evidence_quote: The model proposes, the policy decides and then the tool call happens.

takeaways.technique: Short-lived scoped capability tokens per action
takeaways.what_they_do: Executors hold no standing credentials; each approved action gets a short-lived capability bound to actor, subject, audience, and TTL, with a receipt recording actor, subject, delegation, plan ID, capability, and requested action.
takeaways.evidence_quote: The executor should not hold standing credentials. It gets a shortlived capability for this approved action

takeaways.what_they_do: Each agent gets an operational identity record: what actor it is, who owns it, what subject it acts for, who delegated authority, exact capabilities, governing policy, and revocation path.
takeaways.evidence_quote: What is the actor? Who owns it? What subject is it acting for? Who delegated the authority?

takeaways.what_they_do: For destructive or high-consequence actions, require an enforceable boundary (scoped access, action-time policy, approval) rather than relying on the model following instructions.
takeaways.evidence_quote: If only the break in the model is deciding to behave, you do not have a control.

takeaways.technique: Treat guardrail/filter output as telemetry, not boundary
takeaways.what_they_do: LLM-based filters and guardrails are useful for observability but are not the security boundary for high-consequence actions; the boundary must live outside the model.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Filters and guardrails are useful telemetry obviously, but they're not the enterprise security boundary

takeaways.what_they_do: Convert a raw ticket into a normalized request capturing who asked, on whose behalf, what capability, what scope, and for how long, before the planner sees evidence or tools.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Trusted intent is not the whole ticket here. Um it is the normalized request
